record_type_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Mosimann and Pontusson (2017) is that the effect of union membership on support for redistribution is most pronounced for high-wage workers who belong to unions that are responsive to the interests of low-wage workers.

targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for reproduction from Mosimann and Pontusson (2017) is that the effect of union membership on support for redistribution is most pronounced for high-wage workers who belong to unions that are responsive to the interests of low-wage workers.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: While the replicated estimate of the difference in predicted probabilities is nearly identical to that of the original study (0.098 vs 0.097), levels exhibit small differences: 0.649 vs 0.608 for union members and 0.552 vs 0.511 for the nonunion members. Because these differences remain small (about 4 percentage points or 6–7 percent in relative terms), they can be attributed to the discrepancies between the reproduction and original regression samples.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Section 24 of the preregistration document (https://osf.io/f8kjt/) suggests several exploratory analyses to test the sensitivity of the replication results to choices made to construct the reproduction sample.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The focal predicted-probability difference was recovered to a negligible difference (.098 versus .097), and the authors explicitly judged this a successful reproduction. Authors describe level differences as small despite an unresolved sample-construction discrepancy. Sensitivity analyses are only suggested, not reported as performed.

reasoning: Reconstructs the original ESS rounds and auxiliary data rather than collecting a fresh sample. The changed analytic sample reflects unresolved construction differences in re-analysis. The report supplies only a surname/year/journal/pages reference for the original: its title and DOI are absent and therefore left empty. Title, project ID and OSF node match the assignment; the report names Victor Gay and Andrew Tyner, but does not name every contributor in supplied metadata.
